card.situation: USGS solicitation for janitorial services at Hammond Bay Biological Station (HBBS), Millersburg, MI — three buildings totaling ~4,958 sq. ft., small business set-aside, evaluated on price and technical/past-performance factors.\nReached the owner because Red Cedar is NAICS 561720 exact-match, SBA-eligible, and holds relevant federal janitorial past performance — but the site is ~1,100 miles from Oklahoma City, triggering the owner's 200-mile distance rule.
reasons_for: Red Cedar is NAICS 561720 exact-match and SBA-eligible for this total small business set-aside, clearing the threshold eligibility bar with no waivers needed [set_aside_note: 'ELIGIBLE — The notice is set aside as Small Business Set Aside - Total, and Red Cedar qualifies as a small business'].

Technical capability is strong across all core scope tasks — office/restroom/floor/glass/carpet cleaning, after-hours scheduling, QCP via CMMS, and CIMS-GB certification — with 19 of 31 requirements fully met [matrix_summary: '19 of 31 requirements met, 7 partial, 3 gap, 2 unknown'].

Three qualifying past-performance references (Oklahoma City Federal Building, state office complex, VA outpatient clinic) are within the five-year window and similar in scope, satisfying the evaluation factor directly [954c262f-e8e3d739-p45-76d7df30].
reasons_against: Hammond Bay Biological Station is ~1,100 miles from Oklahoma City, hard-exceeding the owner's 200-mile operational limit, and the firm has no Michigan workforce or regional presence, making reliable performance mobilization undemonstrated [profile: rc-distance owner rule disqualifier].

Travel and mobilization costs from Oklahoma to Michigan would load the firm's price far above local Michigan competitors, creating a fatal disadvantage under the best-value price-and-technical evaluation [954c262f-e8e3d739-p46-c8615f6a].
The proposal deadline of 2026-09-07T12:00:00-06:00 has already passed (days to close = -6.7), so no conforming offer can be submitted in time [954c262f-e8e3d739-p47-ea6c6aa6].

drafts.capability_statement:
Red Cedar Facility Services — Capability Statement
NAICS 561720 | Small Business | WOSB | EDWOSB

Red Cedar Facility Services is a Woman-Owned Small Business providing commercial and federal janitorial and custodial services under NAICS 561720. We are SBA-certified and fully eligible for this total small business set-aside.

Our core capabilities align directly with the HBBS scope:
• Office, lobby, stairway, and common-area cleaning
• Restroom sanitation using disinfectant cleaners, with infection-control protocols drawn from healthcare housekeeping experience
• Floor care: sweeping, mopping, buffing, and carpet cleaning
• Glass and window cleaning
• After-hours scheduled service on recurring weekly and multi-day frequencies

Quality & Compliance:
Red Cedar holds CIMS-GB certification, operates a documented Quality Control Program with inspections logged in a CMMS, and employs OSHA 30-certified supervisors. We maintain a Key Control Program and a green cleaning program using chemicals that will not damage floors, coverings, woodwork, or furniture. All employees are enrolled in e-Verify. We can submit a written Quality Control Plan at the time of proposal submission.

Past Performance (NAICS 561720, within five years):
• Custodial services, Oklahoma City Federal Building (GSA Region 7)
• Janitorial services, state office complex
• Housekeeping support, VA outpatient clinic

We carry general liability and workers' compensation insurance and can provide three past-performance references with points of contact upon request.

Contracting Officer: Yvette Sornberger | Notice: 954c262f233a4f9395857c3532e599bf

reader.scope_summary: The government is buying janitorial services at the USGS Hammond Bay Biological Station (HBBS), covering three buildings: a wet lab (1,551 sq. ft.), an office building (1,851 sq. ft. plus 788 sq. ft. annex), and a sterilization building (768 sq. ft.), each with distinct service frequencies varying by season. The contractor must provide all labor, travel, administration, supervision, supplies, and equipment (except those items specifically provided by the Government) to perform janitorial services including cleaning of offices, restrooms, common areas, floors, glass surfaces, and carpets. Work is performed after normal business hours and the contractor must maintain a quality control program, a key control program, and an on-call representative available 24/7.
reader.evaluation_basis: Award shall be made to the vendor whose offer, conforming to this RFQ, is determined to be the most advantageous to the government, based on price and the other non-price factors listed above; non-price factors include Technical Capability (3-page narrative) and Past Performance (up to three references, similar scope, past five years).
quotes: The Contractor shall provide all labor, travel, administration, supervision, supplies, and equipment (except those items specifically provided by the Government as referenced in this document) to perform janitorial services at the HBBS.
This work shall include the cleaning of three buildings.

In the wet lab building (Attachment A is 1,551 sq. ft.) janitorial services shall be provided 3 days each week, Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, during the months of April, May, June, July, August, and September, and twice a week on Wednesday and Friday during the months of January, February, March, October, November, December, (except Federal holidays and emergencies), after normal business hours (8:00 am and 4:30 pm), unless

In the office building (Attachment B is 1,851 sq. ft. and Attachment B-1 is 788 sq. ft.) janitorial services shall be provided once a week, on Wednesday, during all months of the year (except Federal holidays and emergencies), after normal business hours (8:00 am and 4:30 pm), unless otherwise agreed by the CO or the COR.

In the sterilization building (Attachment C is 768 sq. ft.) janitorial services shall be provide once a week, on Wednesday, during the months of April, May, June, July, August, and September, and no days January, February, March, October, November, and December (except Federal holidays and emergencies), after normal business hours (8:00 am and 4:30 pm), unless otherwise agreed by the CO or the COR.
The award shall be made to the vendor whose offer, conforming to this RFQ, is determined to be the most advantageous to the government, based on price and the other non-price factors listed above.
The following factors shall be used to evaluate offers:
Your quote package shall address each of these factors, as they are the standards against which your quote will be evaluated.

(ii) Past Performance – The offeror must submit past project information similar in scope over the past five (5) years, no more than three (3) past project references, including both prime and subcontractor.
This QCP shall be submitted at the time of proposal submission and updated as required.

The Government shall furnish the necessary equipment and supplies, including but not limited to the following: vacuum cleaner(s) and attachments; floor buffer(s); wax stripper(s); floor wax, toilet bowl cleaners; disinfectant; window and glass cleaner; cleaning brushes, mops; cleaning pads; other cleansers as required; toilet paper; paper towels; hand and liquid soap; napkins; toilet cakes; and trash can liners.
Award shall be made to the vendor whose quote, conforming to this RFQ is determined to be the most advantages to the government.

The award for this requirement shall be made using the policies in the Federal Acquisition Regulations (FAR) Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, and in conjunction with the policies and procedures for solicitation, evaluation, and award prescribed in FAR 13.5 Simplified Procedures for Certain Commercial Items, as appropriate for this acquisition.
